chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Hail cannot be eaten, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
'He afflicts with it whomsoever He wills.' [Quran 13:13]

key_terms.الْبَرَد: Hail (barad) — frozen precipitation, used in classical Arabic for both hail and cold. Here it clearly refers to hailstones.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (Azza wa Jalla) — a standard epithet for God in classical Islamic texts
key_terms.يُصِيبُ: Afflicts, strikes, causes to befall — the Quranic verb describing God's use of hail as a means of punishment

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat hail in Islam according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that hail is not permissible to eat, grounding the prohibition in a Quranic verse (13:13) that describes hail as a divine instrument of punishment dispatched by God's will. This jurisprudential ruling reflects the Shia interpretive method of deriving legal rulings from the Quran's cosmological descriptions — the fact that Allah uses hail as a punitive tool is understood to place it in a category that humans should not consume.
